doc.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Moses's Story of Moses and Homage to John Coltrane for Owl
summary: He was 'the burning bush' on a Moses record; a Paris Meditations concert led Owl Records to commission his Coltrane tribute.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Got to be careful about that stuff. Another Moses date for Gramavision, The Story of Moses.

Story of Moses, great record. I’m the burning bush. You know what he did with me? Soprano, and Don on congas – Alias. He said, “Is it okay if I put an effect on you?” I said sure. He double-timed me, so that I’m like [Liebman imitates the sound]. We just played duo. Then he double-timed me on the soprano. He doubled the speed. Something like that. Yeah, I was the burning bush.
Homage to John Coltrane, which Caris is on.
This is the record that got the award in France that year.

And this is the beginning of my relationship with Owl Records. That came out of the first Meditations concert in Paris. We did a concert at Billancourt, a suburb of Paris. This is what I was talking about yesterday. They wanted Ascension. She transcribed Meditations. We did Meditations. After that, the producer of Owl Records came up to me that night, and he said, “I want to record you. Could you do Coltrane?” I had not done Coltrane yet. I said, “I have not done Coltrane in my career except for Your Lady on the Drum Ode record.” I said, “I think I’m ready to do it. I want to do electric
and acoustic, and I want to change the music around.” That’s how that date came out. That’s a good record. A lot of thought went in that. I wanted to come up with my own way of doing Trane.
